newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA TO CLARIFY FARM TARIFF POLICY - HANEKOM.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA TO CLARIFY FARM TARIFF POLICY - HANEKOM.

text.p: The agriculture department is working on a new trade tariff policy which will address such issues as alleged dumping of American chickens in South Africa, Land and Agriculture Minister Derek Hanekom said on Tuesday.
"A much clearer policy will emerge which will govern the implementation of tariffs," Hanekom told a meeting of a parliamentary committee on agriculture.

He was responding to a question from Inkatha Freedom Party member Jurie Mentz, who said subsidised American chicken imports were destroying efforts by small black poultry producers to expand their businesses.

"Small farmers... in the rural areas are now producing poultry for sale but they are faced with American poultry being brought into the country at 50 percent what it costs to produce them," Mentz said.
Hanekom replied that tariffs would be applied to prevent genuine dumping, but added: "We cannot be artificially protecting industries that cannot be competitive."
